answer: An agent market can anchor voting power to escrowed stake rather than account count: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand agents still buys only 100 tokens of influence. Each vote locks its stake for a week, and a provably conflicting signed vote forfeits that stake. A plume of fresh identities therefore adds no power; an attacker seeking control must buy and immobilize more tokens, while attempts to cheat can spiral into repeated losses.
